title: Limitations — Crew Oxygen System

issue.reason: Issue B. Earlier issues are not held in this dataset.

abstract: Flight crew limitations for the crew oxygen system, covering the minimum pressure for departure, the mask donning requirement and the condition of the stowed mask assembly.

sections.purpose: This entry gives the limitations that apply to the crew oxygen system before departure and in flight, and the crew check that confirms the mask is usable.
sections.description: The crew oxygen system supplies the flight crew masks from a single cylinder through a regulator at each station. The pressure available is displayed on the systems page and must be checked against the table for the number of crew and the planned flight. Each mask is stowed in a box at its station and must be able to be taken out and donned with one hand. The supply hose runs from the regulator to the stowage and lies within the console; a hose that is trapped, twisted or damaged where it lies in the stowage can prevent the mask being withdrawn cleanly, which is why the preflight check is a physical withdrawal and not a visual inspection of the box.
sections.crew_procedure: During the preflight check at each station, check the oxygen pressure against the table, open the stowage box, withdraw the mask with one hand and confirm free movement of the hose, then check the flow with the test slide and stow the mask correctly. If the mask does not withdraw freely, or if the hose shows damage where it lies in the stowage, the station is unserviceable and the aeroplane must not depart with that station occupied.
sections.limitation_note: Minimum crew oxygen pressure for departure is given in the limitations table and depends on the number of flight crew and the planned flight time. Departure with a crew mask that cannot be withdrawn and donned with one hand is not permitted at an occupied station.

type_data.crew_action: Withdraw and don the mask with one hand at each occupied station during the preflight check.
